newsitem.title: USA: Mass. speaker ready to use GOs for convention site.
newsitem.headline: Mass. speaker ready to use GOs for convention site.

text.p: Massachusetts House Speaker Thomas Finneran at a state house press conference Wednesday said he would be willing to use general obligation bonds to finance up to 50 percent of the cost of a new convention center for Boston now estimated to cost up to $700 million.

Finneran, speaking to reporters after delivering a formal address to the Legislature, said the change from his previous position, which required the convention center to be "100 percent financed by revenues from taxes on hotels, motels, rental cars, taxis and the like" was a measure of "good-faith."
He was now willing "to provide some financing from GO (general obligation) debt."
Finneran later said he would still like to see at least half the financing come from revenue sources.

A report released on Monday by a panel formed to study the issue of a new convention center estimated the 600,000 square foot proposed facility would cost up to $645 million and recommended the state allot an additional $50 million to purchase land for further expansion of the facility.
During his House speech, Finneran also said the legislature must address "the extraordinarily high cost of unemployment insurance borne by every single employer in Massachusetts..."

Lexington-based Raytheon Co lost a 20-year contract worth $5 billion to an Arizona company, in part because of the high cost of unemployment insurance the diversified commerical manufactuer and defense contractor must bear.
"We're a high cost state. We will always be a high cost state, but we have to lower our costs," he told reporters later.

Finneran added the "equitable tax treatment of domestic insurance companies, utility de-regulation and the costs of capital formation "as warranting attention during this legislative session. He told reporters the later referred specifically to Massachusetts' 12 percent tax on unearned income. He told legislators he would like the house to complete debate and pass a House budget during the week of April 14.
